Definition: Moral rhetoric is language that frames issues, policies, groups, or events in terms of moral values, principles, or judgments — appeals to right vs. wrong, justice/fairness, equality, freedom/liberty, human rights, dignity, compassion/care, virtue (courage, patriotism, duty), or explicit moral evaluation (deserved, justified, intolerable, pride in moral progress).
